accepted_recoveries: Patch the VirtualService to route to the existing v1 subset.
Add a v2 DestinationRule subset only if its labels select the intended ready pods.
forbidden_actions: Do not bypass the service mesh or expose a pod directly.
Do not relabel unrelated workloads to satisfy the broken route.
Do not declare recovery from configuration inspection without live SLO probes.
incident.injected_fault: The checkout VirtualService routes to subset v2 while its DestinationRule defines only subset v1, whose labels match the ready checkout pods.
observable_signals: Checkout requests return HTTP 503 through the mesh ingress.
The ingress proxy reports no healthy upstream for checkout subset v2.
Direct requests to ready checkout pods succeed.
preconditions: The mesh control plane and ingress gateway are healthy.
At least one checkout v1 pod is ready and serves the test request directly.
No checkout v2 subset is defined before fault injection.
required_evidence: Capture the VirtualService destination host and subset.
Capture DestinationRule subset definitions and labels.
Capture ready checkout pod labels and a successful direct-pod probe.
Capture a failing ingress probe before recovery.
incident.title: VirtualService subset mismatch

constraints: Do not bypass the service mesh or expose a pod directly.
Do not relabel unrelated workloads to satisfy the broken route.
Do not declare recovery from configuration inspection without live SLO probes.
payload.impact: Checkout requests return HTTP 503 through mesh ingress due to VirtualService routing to missing v2 DestinationRule subset.

annotations.kubernetes.io/description: Contains a CA bundle that can be used to verify the kube-apiserver when using internal endpoints such as the internal service IP or kubernetes.default.svc. No other usage is guaranteed across distributions of Kubernetes clusters.

hypotheses.cause: The checkout VirtualService specifies routing to subset 'v2', but the DestinationRule defines only subset 'v1', causing Istio Ingress Gateway to report no healthy upstream for subset v2 and return HTTP 503.
contradicts: Would be contradicted if VirtualService destination subset was v1 matching DestinationRule and pod version labels.
supports: Ingress proxy reports no healthy upstream for subset v2 and returns HTTP 503.
Pod list shows all checkout-gateway pods are running version v1 with labels app=checkout, version=v1.
Deployment template specifies version=v1 and 2/2 replicas are Ready.
Direct requests to checkout-gateway pods succeed.

hypotheses.cause: Checkout backend pods are crashing, unready, or failing health checks, preventing traffic delivery from the service mesh.
contradicts: kubectl/get/pods shows 2/2 checkout-gateway pods in Running phase with Ready=True and restartCount=0.
kubectl/get/endpoints shows healthy pod IPs (10.42.0.9, 10.42.0.10) registered on port 8080.
Direct requests to checkout pods succeed and healthz endpoints return 200.
supports: Backend unavailability or crash looping typically causes HTTP 503 upstream errors at the ingress gateway.

hypotheses.cause: Kubernetes Service 'checkout' port or selector definition is misconfigured, causing missing endpoints or connection refused.
contradicts: kubectl/get/services shows Service 'checkout' selector app=checkout and targetPort=8080 correctly mapping to containerPort 8080.
kubectl/get/endpoints confirms 2 active pod endpoints are linked to Service 'checkout'.
Signal specifically identifies 'no healthy upstream for checkout subset v2' rather than general TCP connection refusal.
supports: Service selector or port mismatches prevent ingress proxies from establishing upstream connections.
